description: #54: the settings name TWO repositories in `[repos]` (`alder`, `birch`) and the ready task is the birch project's, so the coordinator passes the project's name as `--clone birch`: not a path and not the other name. Two graders read the call and one reads the tree it cut. The tree grader alone cannot tell a name from a path, since `--clone birch-checkout` cuts the same tree; the call graders do. The harness builds one repository, so only `birch-checkout` is one: `alder-checkout` is a plain directory the fixture carries, and the wrong name fails on that too. The prompt asks for a dry-run worker launch so no worker process starts.
prompt: Start the birch security audit. For this isolated test, use --dry-run for the worker launch and do not start a real worker process.

graders.name: a worktree call passes the project's name
graders.rule: `<repo>` is the repository's name in the settings' `[repos]` table when the table names it, otherwise its path.

graders.name: no worktree call passes any other clone value
graders.rule: `<repo>` is the repository's name in the settings' `[repos]` table when the table names it, otherwise its path.

graders.name: the tree that was cut belongs to the project's repository
graders.rule: `<repo>` is the repository's name in the settings' `[repos]` table when the table names it, otherwise its path.
